title: Midterm candidate: cumulative evidence and models

questions.prompt: Ionizable substitution in an assembly. Authored form A. A fictional protein has a aspartate side chain on a water-exposed surface at pH 7; its measured pKa is 4. It is changed to alanine. Other covalent bonds remain intact; assembly has not been measured.

response_fields.prompt: Which description distinguishes the mutation from ordinary molecular association?
options: The mutation only changes noncovalent contacts, never structure.
Association necessarily changes every peptide bond.
The side-chain covalent structure changes; reversible association can occur without new covalent bonds.

response_fields.prompt: What bounded prediction follows at the specified pH?
options: Alanine adds an ionized carboxylate at pH 7.
The original side chain is predominantly negative; alanine removes that charge and may change assembly.
Charge loss proves the protein cannot assemble.

response_fields.prompt: Which chemical feature is directly removed by this substitution?
options: Every backbone amide.
The side-chain carboxyl group, without necessarily removing the backbone amide.
A side-chain phosphate that neither residue contains.

questions.prompt: A titratable group in water. Authored form A. An isolated carboxyl group in water has pKa 4.5; the solution pH is 3.5. Use [A-]/[HA] = 10^(pH-pKa), with no coupled groups. A separate nonpolar solute aggregates in water without new covalent bonds.

response_fields.prompt: Which interpretation of the nonpolar aggregate is justified?
options: Water-mediated hydrophobic association is plausible; aggregation alone does not establish covalent bonding.
Nonpolar solutes must become permanently charged.
Aggregation proves new peptide bonds form.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate the ratio of deprotonated to protonated group on a bare ratio scale. Report exactly 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Protein quantity and function. Authored form A. A buried hydrophobic residue is replaced by a charged residue. In matched recovered protein, reference abundance is 100 and variant abundance is 50 arbitrary amount units. Total activities are 800 and 400 arbitrary rate units. Folding measurements and localization are missing.

response_fields.prompt: Which prediction respects residue environment and missing measurements?
options: Any charged substitution necessarily increases native folding.
A buried charge may disrupt stability or packing, but the actual fold and localization need measurement.
A buried charge proves loss of all activity in every context.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate variant/reference specific activity: (variant activity/amount)/(reference activity/amount), a bare ratio. Report exactly 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Passive potassium and transport classes. Authored form A. Only K+ is permeant in an ideal membrane. Inside K+ is 100 mM; outside is 10 mM; at 37 C use E_K = 61.5 log10(outside/inside) mV. Membrane voltage is 0 mV. A separate carrier moves a substrate uphill only when coupled to ATP hydrolysis.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate E_K using the stipulated rounded coefficient. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Classify the ATP-dependent uphill carrier.
options: Passive transport because all carriers are passive.
Simple diffusion through the lipid bilayer.
Active transport; downhill carrier-mediated flux would be facilitated diffusion.

questions.prompt: Compartment boundary evidence. Authored form A. A fictional protein with a cleavable ER-targeting peptide enters a lumen. Intact vesicles protect 82% of its immunoreactivity from added protease; detergent plus protease removes the signal. A cytosolic marker is digested without detergent. Vesicle recovery is matched. These are biochemical aliquots, not independent living cells.

response_fields.prompt: What topology follows if the stated targeting and translocation succeed?
options: The protein must cross the bilayer at every secretory step.
A cleaved ER peptide necessarily places the mature protein in the nucleus.
The mature soluble protein is on the luminal side and remains topologically outside the cytosol.

response_fields.prompt: What is the bounded protease conclusion?
options: Protection proves a unique living-cell organelle and direct binding.
Protection is consistent with enclosed antigen; detergent sensitivity and markers address integrity, not exact native location by themselves.
The cytosolic digestion control is interchangeable with vesicle integrity.

questions.prompt: Receptor recycling and cargo sorting. Authored form A. Pulse-labeled extracellular cargo binds equally to reference and perturbed cells at time zero. At a matched chase, receptor returns to the surface in both; cargo in a degradative compartment changes from 60% to 20%. Total recovered label and new synthesis are matched, but degradation fragments and spatial resolution are not measured.

response_fields.prompt: Which route preserves topology?
options: A surface receptor and all its cargo must always share their terminal destination.
Recycling requires cargo to become cytosolic by membrane inversion.
Endocytosed luminal cargo can remain enclosed while its receptor recycles to the surface.

response_fields.prompt: What can the matched measurements support?
options: A late compartment percentage proves changed transcription.
Equal initial binding proves normal sorting and degradation.
A redistribution consistent with altered sorting; unresolved label loss and compartment assignment still need controls.

questions.prompt: Catalysis and coupling. Authored form A. Use v = Vmax*S/(Km+S), with Vmax 80 arbitrary rate units, Km 2 mM and S 2 mM. At matched conditions reaction X has deltaG +12 kJ/mol and coupled reaction Y has deltaG -20 kJ/mol; stoichiometry is 1:1.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate v on the declared bare rate-unit scale. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Calculate the net deltaG per mole of coupled events. Report exactly 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Active enzyme and equilibrium. Authored form A. A purified catalyst changes the activation barrier without changing initial/final state free energies. In an ideal initial-rate assay active enzyme is 2 nM, kcat 10 per second, S 4 mM and Km 4 mM; v = kcat*E*S/(Km+S). No inhibition or enzyme loss occurs.

response_fields.prompt: Which effect is compatible with a catalyst?
options: A catalyst makes every uphill reaction have a negative deltaG.
Faster forward and reverse equilibration with unchanged equilibrium constant for the same states.
A catalyst changes equilibrium by consuming itself irreversibly.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate initial v on a bare nM-per-second scale. Report exactly 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Inhibitor model and optical control. Authored form A. An initial-rate fit gives Vmax 100 and apparent Km 4 mM with inhibitor; use v=Vmax*S/(Km+S) at S 2 mM. Without inhibitor Vmax is the same and Km is smaller. Blank wells show negligible optical interference; direct binding and uncertainty estimates are unavailable.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate the fitted inhibited initial rate on the bare rate-unit scale. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Which statement is warranted by the parameter pattern and controls?
options: It is consistent with an ideal competitive pattern; the fit and optical blank do not prove a molecular binding route.
An optical blank proves a particular active-site structure.
The pattern proves irreversible enzyme destruction.

questions.prompt: Sampling and overlap. Authored form A. For a conventional image estimate lateral resolution d=0.61*lambda/NA with lambda 500 nm and NA 1. Sample-plane pixel size is 100 nm. Two fluorescent channels overlap within the optical spot; single-label controls show measurable bleed-through.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate nominal lateral resolution in nm. This estimate is distinct from pixel size. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Which follow-up and conclusion fit this image?
options: Increase magnification and declare direct binding from overlap.
Correct spectral cross-talk with matched controls; overlap at optical resolution does not establish direct molecular binding.
Discard single-label controls because colors differ on screen.

questions.prompt: Recovery and enrichment. Authored form A. Input target marker activity is 200 units; the collected fraction contains 80 units. Fraction total protein is 2 mg. A second compartment marker is also detected. Only one collected fraction is supplied; missing fractions and rupture controls are absent.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate target-marker recovery as a percentage of input. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Which design can address the current limitations?
options: Treat the fraction protein mass as a count of independent cultures.
Use only the target marker and call the fraction pure.
Collect all fractions and input for mass balance, multiple compartment markers and integrity controls; enrichment alone is not purity.

questions.prompt: Polarity and isotope generations. Authored form A. The template is 5-prime GACTA 3-prime. Polymerase extends a primer by adding to its 3-prime end. After heavy-to-light transfer, controlled isotope-density generation 1 has only hybrid-density DNA and generation 2 has hybrid plus light DNA; density resolution controls pass.

response_fields.prompt: Which description correctly preserves strand polarity and synthesis?
options: Polymerase makes the leading strand by adding to its 5-prime end.
Both aligned strands have the same 5-prime to 3-prime direction.
The aligned complement runs 3-prime to 5-prime; a newly made strand grows 5-prime to 3-prime, with fragments on the lagging side.

response_fields.prompt: Which model fits the specified resolved generations?
options: All three models predict exactly the same resolved generations.
Conservative replication predicts only hybrid DNA in generation 1.
Semiconservative replication; the second generation helps distinguish the ideal dispersive prediction.

questions.prompt: Lesion signal and repair. Authored form A. A bulky-adduct assay has matched input and extraction standards. At a fixed time lesion signal is 20 units in reference and 60 in a repair perturbation; rescue brings it near reference. Mutation counts, survival and independent pathway activity are unmeasured.

response_fields.prompt: Which distinction and pathway hypothesis is appropriate?
options: Polymerase proofreading acts during synthesis; bulky-adduct excision is a plausible different repair pathway requiring specific tests.
Every bulky lesion is removed solely by polymerase proofreading.
Proofreading and post-replicative mismatch repair are the same timed process.

response_fields.prompt: What does the rescue support within these measurements?
options: Perturbation-associated lesion-signal change; mutation frequency and a unique native mechanism remain unmeasured.
Rescue proves zero off-target effects or survival selection.
A lesion signal is directly the mutation frequency per genome.

questions.prompt: Chromatin and independent units. Authored form A. Four independent cultures per state are each split into three technical aliquots. Accessibility rises by 40% and matched RNA by 25% between states. A histone mark also increases; no endogenous element perturbation has been done.

response_fields.prompt: Which chromatin interpretation is bounded?
options: Nucleosomes never alter accessibility.
Any mark increase proves an irreversible transcriptional switch.
Accessibility and a mark can be associated with state; a mark is not by itself a transcriptional switch.

response_fields.prompt: Which analysis and causal follow-up fit the units?
options: Treat twelve aliquots as twelve independent cultures and infer causality from correlation.
Summarize aliquots within four cultures per state and perturb the endogenous element with matched controls and RNA/readout follow-up.
Use a plasmid alone to prove endogenous element necessity.

questions.prompt: Expression and controls. Authored form A. A fictional construct is transcribed to mRNA and translated to protein. Three independent cultures have background-corrected reporter values 10, 12, 14; an untreated reference mean is 8. Positive assay control and a no-reporter negative control pass; input/loading measurements are not supplied.

response_fields.prompt: Which information path fits the model?
options: RNA synthesis and peptide synthesis are the same chemical reaction.
Protein must first be reverse translated directly into genomic DNA.
DNA is transcribed to RNA; ribosomes read an mRNA frame to synthesize a polypeptide.

response_fields.prompt: Which control is missing for an abundance-normalized comparison?
options: A matched input/loading measurement; positive and negative controls address different assay questions.
No loading control is needed because the reporter is fluorescent.
A second positive control automatically replaces loading.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate the descriptive difference between the culture mean and reference on the bare reporter scale. Report exactly 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: ChIP input and cis claims. Authored form A. The measured input aliquot is fraction 0.01 of total input; Ct_input 20, Ct_IP 22. Under equal doubling efficiency use percent input=100*fraction*2^(Ct_input-Ct_IP). IgG and negative-locus controls pass. A matched plasmid deletion lowers reporter output; the endogenous locus has not been edited.

response_fields.prompt: Calculate simplified ChIP percent input. Report exactly 3 significant figures.
Which inference separates the two assays?
options: IgG controls replace input and PCR efficiency controls.
ChIP plus plasmid deletion proves direct binding and endogenous necessity.
Enrichment supports occupancy-associated evidence and the plasmid tests sequence activity in that context; neither alone proves direct binding or endogenous necessity.
